name: Dassault Falcon 2000
summary: Twin-engine derivative of the Falcon 900 with the same wide cabin cross-section, popular with US corporate and fractional (NetJets) fleets.

wings: Low swept wing; blended winglets on the LX/S/LXS
engines: Two turbofans (CFE738 or PW308C) in pods on the rear fuselage
No third engine in the tail
fuselage: Wide fuselage with a long pointed nose and rounded-rectangle windows
tail: Cruciform tail: horizontal stabilizer partway up the swept fin, not on top
Clean fin root without an intake

tellTales: Tailplane set partway up the fin on a large twinjet
Clean fin root without any intake, only two engine pods
Wide fuselage with a long pointed nose

confusedWith.howToTell: The Falcon 2000 has two engines and a clean fin root; the Falcon 50/900/7X/8X has a third engine with an intake at the base of the fin.
The Falcon 2000's tailplane is partway up the fin; the Challenger 600 has a T-tail.
The Falcon 2000 is larger with rounded-rectangle windows; the Hawker 800 is smaller with oval windows and a big belly fairing.
The Falcon 20 is an older design with small round windows, plain wingtips and a low-set tailplane; the Falcon 2000 has oval windows and a cruciform tail.
